A flash flood triggered by a breached landslide dam along central Nepal's Budhi Gandaki river has swept away roughly three dozen homes, four bridges, and a hydropower construction site. As mass evacuations continue, the Nepali army has rescued 49 stranded residents, with five people still reported missing amid widespread damage to power and communication lines.

Nepali authorities said 903 people had died, with 4,247 missing, after last week's Himalayan flood that carved a trail of destruction in the country's valley towns and villages.  The Nepali army said search-and-rescue teams were using controlled blasts, excavators and searchlights to clear water and mud and reach trapped people.  Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the flood was an ‘unprecedented and devastating natural disaster’ and it remained challenging to compile a complete assessment of the damage. #nepal #asia #flood #himalayas #news

🚨Shocking visuals coming from Nepal's Gorkha District today. A massive, black debris-filled flood surged down the Budhi Gandaki River early this morning after a landslide blocked the river in Chumnubri village. The temporary dam suddenly burst, unleashing a wall of water, mud and rocks. In the video you can see entire buildings with green roofs being swallowed in seconds as people watch helplessly from the hilltop. According to authorities, more than 35-65 houses in Salleri Bazaar, Jagat, Paiyuka and riverbed settlements have been swept away. At least 4 bridges including 2 motorable bridges were destroyed. 5 to 10 people are reported missing so far, and 49 people have been rescued and airlifted by the Nepal Army. A RED ALERT has been issued for downstream districts - Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi. Residents are being urged to stay away from the river and move to high ground. This comes just 2 months after the deadly August flood in Nepal that killed over 1,400 people. Pray for Nepal. 🙏 #NepalFlood #PrayForNepal #Gorkha #FlashFlood #NepalNews

A massive landslide occurred in Lete, Mustang, after part of the hillside suddenly collapsed. However, the area remains at risk following the landslide, and locals and travelers have been urged to stay alert, exercise caution and follow safety precautions.
